proposalRationale:
TJR chart timezone: all session levels are computed in New York (Eastern) time.

CLASSIFICATION: SOURCE-STATED, and unusually well supported for this corpus -- 2 supporting
evidence items, 0 contradicting, plus a stated failure mode (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|058: marking
session levels on a non-Eastern chart puts them at the wrong times and makes the strategy appear
not to work) and a stated reason (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|056: sessions are defined in the market's
own time zone).

MECHANICAL SPECIFICATION: every session boundary timestamp is resolved in IANA zone
America/New_York, with the DST offset resolved for the specific instant being converted rather
than a fixed UTC offset. The NYSE regular session opens 09:30 America/New_York
(CLAIM|TJR|20260727|057) and pre-market starts 08:30 (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|003).

DATA REQUIRED: an IANA timezone database (Intl.DateTimeFormat is sufficient) and the instrument's
timestamped candle series. No market data beyond timestamps.

FALSIFICATION: recompute a set of session-open levels under America/New_York and under a fixed
UTC-5 offset across a US DST transition date. If the levels are identical on transition days, the
rule has no observable content; if they differ, confirm against TJR's charted levels which one
matches. This is decidable from data alone with no discretion.

NOTE ON SCOPE MISMATCH (material, and not currently recorded as a contradiction): this claim is
in tension with the SHIPPED engine's scope rather than with another claim. TJR trades US indices,
S&P 500 and NASDAQ (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|001), on New York sessions. MOGO's implemented Phase 1
engine resolves ASIAN/LONDON/NEW_YORK boundaries in Europe/London and is exercised on FX pairs
(GBP_USD in the fixtures). The engine is therefore NOT an implementation of this claim, and its
passing tests are not evidence for it. Recorded here rather than silently reconciled.

UNKNOWN: (a) TJR's exact session-open times for the Asian and London sessions are not stated in
the corpus at all -- only the New York 08:30/09:30 figures are; (b) whether "session high/low"
means the regular-hours range or includes pre-market is unstated; (c) no source statement covers
half-days or exchange holidays.
